title: LP2-00–55: LP2-15 spiral-prime shifts
question: Does the sixteen-prime LP2-15 spiral, repeated as modulo-29 shifts, recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings on LP2-00–55?
summary: A cyclic shift stream from all sixteen LP2-15 spiral primes yields 1760 distinct page outputs and no exact match to nine fixed 12-rune openings.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Repeat the sixteen panel-derived primes in spiral order as modulo-29 shifts, with addition and subtraction, and compare first twelve output indices to nine fixed openings.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–15; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 1760 cases and 15840 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other page starts, noncyclic use, reversed or reordered spiral, prime-index values, interruptions, heading removal, word or row resets, cross-page carry and language scoring.

finding: Zero fixed-opening matches among 1760 distinct complete page outputs. The independent checker reconstructs all sixteen primes from the panel ledger and inverts every transformed rune.
limitations: The shift operation and cyclic repetition are added assumptions, not instructions printed on LP2-15. Only nine fixed 12-rune beginnings are tested; this does not rule out other uses of the panel or other cipher classes. Computational review only; human review pending.
next_steps: A different panel operation needs its own frozen route, advancement and evaluation rule; do not treat the absence of these nine openings as a global exclusion of the spiral clue.
